Checked on jfs-components 0.1.60 (2026-09-23); the installed package is 0.1.78. Re-check before relying on it.

The Avatar guide and its evidence were checked on 23 September 2026 on jfs-components 0.1.60 (its Sources note still says so); the installed package is 0.1.78 (mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02). Read against the installed Avatar.tsx and Skeleton.tsx, every sentence this entry quotes still holds, but loading no longer needs a SkeletonGroup: Avatar draws its same-size placeholder when loading is true on its own (Avatar.tsx lines 167 and 224, visible={loading === true}; Skeleton.tsx lines 134 and 272–275). So the States description (“Loading is a runtime state supplied through SkeletonGroup, not a style or size variant.”), the Sources line (“Loading replaces Avatar content with a neutral, token-backed Skeleton inside an active SkeletonGroup.”) and the evidence (“a direct `loading={true}` outside an active `SkeletonGroup` renders no placeholder”) say less than the package; the entry follows the package’s loading fact and doesn’t quote them. Re-check the guide on 0.1.78 and publish it, then re-extract. Added by Claude Code in the overnight run agentpack-batch11, for Marcin to confirm. Guide fix #533.

summary: Represent one person or account with an image or initials.

useWhen.text: Represent one person or account with an image or initials.

from.quote: Represent one person or account with an image or initials.

useWhen.text: Identify an account owner at a glance.

from.quote: Identify an account owner at a glance

avoidWhen.text: Showing different people with the Image style and no imageSource: they all get the same bundled fallback and can't be told apart. Use a portrait or clear initials instead.

from.quote: Both images resolve to the same bundled fallback and cannot distinguish separate identities.

anatomy.holds: Avatar Size sets the token-owned width and height; its default radius resolves to a circle.

from.quote: Avatar Size sets the token-owned width and height; its default radius resolves to a circle.

anatomy.holds: The Monogram style centers the supplied text and uses Avatar label tokens.

from.quote: The Monogram style centers the supplied text and uses Avatar label tokens.

anatomy.holds: The Image style crops a supplied image source into the same circular frame.

from.quote: The Image style crops a supplied image source into the same circular frame.

placementAdvice.text: A surrounding Card may add a name or role when the layout calls for it; Avatar does not require nearby text.

from.quote: A surrounding Card may add a name or role when the layout calls for it; Avatar does not require nearby text.

placementAdvice.text: A surrounding card or row can give it room, but doesn't stretch it: its size comes from Avatar Size.

from.quote: A surrounding card or row can provide room, but it does not stretch Avatar automatically.

configuration.text: Use a real image when available; use a short monogram otherwise.

from.quote: Use a real image when available; use a short monogram otherwise.

configuration.text: style selects which content is rendered: Monogram shows its monogram text; Image shows imageSource, or the package fallback when there is none.

from.quote: Style selects which content is rendered. Monogram uses its text property; Image uses imageSource and otherwise shows the package fallback.

configuration.text: style is Image by default: set style="Monogram" to show initials.
Image: provide an image source that represents this person. The bundled fallback is only a preview when no source is supplied.

from.quote: Provide an image source that represents this person. The bundled fallback is only a preview when no source is supplied.

configuration.text: Monogram: use a short, recognizable set of initials when a portrait is not available.

from.quote: Use a short, recognizable set of initials when a portrait is not available.

configuration.text: Pick one of the four Avatar Size modes: L 42 px, M 36 px, S 29 px or XS 14 px.

from.quote: Pick one of the four Avatar Size modes

configuration.text: With no Avatar Size set, an Avatar is L, 42 px.
loading true shows a same-size circular placeholder instead of the avatar; left unset, it follows the surrounding SkeletonGroup.

rules.text: Set style to Image or Monogram, then supply the matching image source or monogram text.

from.quote: Set Style to Image or Monogram, then supply the matching image source or monogram text.

rules.text: Use monogram text: supply initials for a compact, text-based identity.

from.quote: Supply initials for a compact text based identity.

rules.text: Supply image content: set imageSource to the intended image.

from.quote: Set imageSource to the intended image.

rules.text: Use one letter at XS (14 px).

from.quote: Use one letter at XS

rules.text: Give every identity meaningful content: each Avatar shows its own portrait or monogram.

from.quote: Each Avatar shows its own portrait or monogram content.

states.when: The image or monogram remains inside the chosen Avatar Size.

from.quote: The image or monogram remains inside the chosen Avatar Size.

states.when: While the image or monogram is unavailable: a same-size, neutral, token-backed Skeleton circle replaces the identity content.

from.quote: It replaces the identity content with a same-size neutral placeholder.

accessibility.text: Don't rely on Avatar to announce who it is or to act as a button: this version drops its typed accessibility label and keeps role image on the press wrapper, so the guide's examples stay non-interactive.

from.quote: This version drops its typed accessibility label and keeps role image on the press wrapper, so examples remain non-interactive.

doDont.do: Use a portrait or clear initials
doDont.dont: Reuse the built-in fallback for different people
doDont.why: Both images resolve to the same bundled fallback and cannot distinguish separate identities.

from.quote: Use a portrait or clear initials

examples.purpose: An account owner in a Card, the guide's In context: a Monogram Avatar beside the owner's role and the account. The Card adds that context; the Avatar itself needs no nearby text. It is at M (36 px), the size the guide's In context card draws in its code (its copy names no size).
examples.jsx:
<Card variant="slim">
  <HStack alignVertical="center">
    <Avatar style="Monogram" monogram="MS" modes={{ 'Avatar Size': 'M' }} />
    <VStack>
      <Card.Title>Account owner</Card.Title>
      <Card.SupportText>Shared savings account</Card.SupportText>
    </VStack>
  </HStack>
</Card>

from.quote: A surrounding Card may add a name or role when the layout calls for it; Avatar does not require nearby text.

examples.purpose: A person's own photo, the Image style (the default) at the default size, L (42 px). The URI stands for the image that represents this person; with no imageSource the Avatar would show the bundled fallback, which is only a preview.

from.quote: Set imageSource to the intended image.

examples.purpose: The smallest size, XS (14 px), with one monogram letter, as the guide's Content shows.

from.quote: The XS example shows a single monogram letter.

props.name: accessibilityLabel
props.description: Accepted by the type but discarded: the implementation hides the inner image and text from accessibility and gives the pressable wrapper role image.

props.name: loading
props.description: Explicit per-instance loading override. When `true`, renders a same-size circular skeleton instead of the avatar. Defaults to inheriting from the surrounding `<SkeletonGroup>`.

props.name: ...Omit<React.ComponentProps<typeof View>, 'style' | 'accessibilityRole' | 'accessibilityLabel'>
props.description: Inherited React Native props the component also accepts. They are not part of the design contract and no guide documents them.
